propositions: The lifespan shutdown drain waits only on queue.join() for webhook-queued reviews, but reconcile_once awaits review_and_vote inline outside the queue, so in-flight reconciler reviews are cancelled within shutdown_cancel_seconds (~10s) rather than drained within shutdown_drain_seconds (~1200s).

Any container stop outside the autodeploy path (manual docker compose, systemd stop, reboot, deploy rollback) kills mid-flight reconciler reviews with no drain, and the reconciler is the retry path for reviews killed by other mechanisms.

The drain must cover in-flight reconciler work by waiting on in_flight_reviews() under the existing shutdown_drain_seconds budget without extending indefinitely or allowing new reviews to start after shutdown begins.
The stop flag _stop_requested outlived shutdown in the adopted design because it was cleared only at lifespan startup, causing post-shutdown reconcile_once calls to silently skip all candidates.

The lifespan drain implementation uses a cooperative request_stop() signal and a shared single deadline on shutdown_drain_seconds, gated on voter.in_flight_reviews(), with the queue drain and reconcile task drain sequenced to keep the existing grace-period invariant.
